content.title: About
content.content: Meat with gravy is a ready‑to‑eat dish consisting of boiled or roasted meat covered with a flavorful thick sauce. Common meats are beef, pork or chicken, and the gravy is made from broth, cream, tomato base or a blend of spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Serving meat with gravy dates back to medieval European kitchens, where gravy was used to moisten dry cuts of meat.
In different regions the gravy can be light (cream‑based) or dark (made from browned meat and tomato paste).
In Japan a similar concept is “nitsuke,” a sauce served with grilled meat.
Gravy helps retain moisture in the meat, keeping it juicy during longer storage.
Some countries add red wine to the gravy, giving it a distinctive aroma.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Meat provides all essential amino acids needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef and pork are high in vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Meat supplies iron, zinc and phosphorus, important for blood formation and bone health.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: Gravy, especially when cream‑based, adds calories, useful for people with higher energy needs.

items.title: Improved nutrient absorption
items.content: Fats in the gravy aid the absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K).

items.title: High fat and calorie content
items.content: Rich creamy gravies can contribute to weight gain if consumed in excess.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Prepared gravies often contain a lot of salt, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some gravies include dairy, gluten or soy, which can trigger allergic reactions.

items.title: Risk of bacterial growth
items.content: Improper storage of cooked meat can lead to pathogen growth, so keep the product refrigerated.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot as a main course, typically with a side of potatoes, rice or vegetables. Reheat in the microwave or on the stovetop, stirring to keep the gravy from separating.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C in an airtight container for up to 3 days. For longer storage freeze at –18 °C, where it remains good for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before consumption.
